content.text:
I submitted index 5 (Sb fraction 0.0896), which gave the highest EQE I measured: 0.0535%. I used all 5 EQE measurements and 3 of the 5 XRD measurements. I can't tell whether it's the best composition on the line, because the region just around it (indices 3, 4 and 7–15) was never measured for EQE.

**EQE results:**

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | 0.090 | **0.0535** |
| 6 | 0.101 | 0.0504 |
| 16 | 0.284 | 0.0380 |
| 24 | 0.516 | 0.0351 |
| 28 | 0.630 | 0.0333 |

- **First guess was wrong:** I started at the Sb-rich end because the model predicted a 2.97 eV band gap for YSbO₄ (Sb fraction 0.5). That is the only known phase here predicted to absorb the 3.2 eV light. But EQE was low and nearly flat from Sb 0.28 to 0.63, and the only higher values were at the Y-rich end.
- **XRD:** Index 6 (Sb 0.10) looked like a single phase. Index 0 (Sb 0.055) and index 11 (Sb 0.17) each showed extra peaks, which suggests a second phase is present. That points to a best region around Sb 0.09–0.10.
- **Last measurement:** A GP model fitted to the EQE data suggested index 12 (Sb 0.19) for the last measurement. I went with index 5, next to the single-phase sample, and it came out on top.

**Not ruled out:**
- The composition trend could keep rising at lower Sb; index 0 is the endpoint and I never measured its EQE.
- The GP gave indices 10–13 (Sb 0.16–0.21) a similar predicted EQE, with large uncertainty.

The EQE gap between indices 5 and 6 is small (0.0535% vs 0.0504%), so the ranking between them may be within measurement noise.
